data.name: VR Amazing Files: Horror Hospital
data.detailed_description:
This is a Room Escape Game


The scary and abandoned hospital is filled with zombies, want to solve the extremely challenging puzzle with low ammo? Just have a try!
All puzzles and weapon systems in this game are carefully designed for a fun experience. You have to save ammo and hope your hands won’t be nervously shaking to drop magazines to the ground.

cues:

  • There are no word puzzles, so all players can successfully play the game regardless of their age or nationality. No language barriers, great!

  • Have a clear understanding of the situation before shooting. Think twice before taking risks, because you can’t count on zombies to give you the time studying how to open the safety catch, right? Forget about killing most zombies, where can you get that much ammo? Just figure out another solution.
  • Don’t act alone in the midnight.
  • Don’t try to reach your head into the walls in the game, because it is painful to hit a virtual wall or real wall. We all know it.
  • Be mindful of all details, because you may find clues there.
  • If you are trapped in somewhere and unable to get out, please come to the forum, and after seeing many other people who also failed to escape, you can definitely feel better, because you are not the only one who may be eaten by the zombies, so stay cool.
  • There may be bugs in the game because our testing personnel has been testing the game with their eyes closed all the time out of fears. They’ll have to wet their pants if they opened eyes to play the game. Therefore, we welcome all players to provide feedback about any problems they met in our game.

reviews.review:
VR Amazing Files: Horror Hospital is a compact virtual reality horror experience that mixes environmental puzzles, exploration, resource management, and encounters with the undead. Developed and published by weyha.com, the game approaches its hospital setting more like a dangerous escape room than a straightforward zombie shooter. Weapons are available, but ammunition is deliberately limited, encouraging players to investigate their surroundings and think carefully before resorting to gunfire. This creates an interesting balance between puzzle solving and survival, where observation can be just as important as having a loaded weapon.

The story places you inside an abandoned hospital while searching for missing research notes connected to Patient No. 0 and the development of a mysterious serum. It is a straightforward setup that primarily exists to justify exploring the facility, but it works well enough for this style of VR horror. Empty medical rooms, confined corridors, unsettling equipment, and wandering zombies provide the atmosphere. Instead of relying on an elaborate narrative with lengthy conversations or cinematic sequences, the experience keeps the player focused on discovering clues and figuring out how to progress deeper into the hospital.

Puzzle solving is one of the more important parts of the experience. Players are expected to inspect their surroundings closely because small environmental details can provide the information needed to continue. The puzzles avoid relying heavily on written language, making them easier to understand through observation and interaction. This is particularly suitable for virtual reality, where physically examining objects and looking around a room feels more natural than constantly reading menus or large blocks of text. It also means that rushing through areas can result in overlooking something important.

Combat is deliberately restrained by ammunition scarcity. Although zombies can be attacked with firearms, attempting to shoot every enemy is not necessarily the best strategy. Limited resources make every encounter a small decision about whether ammunition should be spent or conserved. This gives the zombies more value as sources of pressure because their purpose is not simply to provide targets. A player who wastes too many rounds can make later situations considerably more uncomfortable. Handling weapons through VR motion controls also adds physical tension, especially when trying to react quickly while an enemy is approaching.

The hospital itself benefits significantly from virtual reality. A relatively ordinary horror environment becomes more intimidating when experienced from a first-person VR perspective. Looking through doorways, turning around after hearing something suspicious, inspecting dark corners, and searching rooms feel more immediate when the player's physical movements correspond with those actions. The game's atmosphere depends heavily on this sense of presence. It may not offer the visual sophistication of newer VR horror releases, but being physically surrounded by the environment helps compensate for some of its technical age.

Its age is nevertheless one of the most noticeable limitations. Released during the earlier period of consumer virtual reality, the game reflects design conventions and production standards that can feel dated compared with modern VR titles. Interactions are relatively straightforward, the scope is modest, and players expecting a lengthy survival-horror adventure may find the experience too limited. It is better approached as a focused VR horror puzzle game rather than something comparable to a full-scale campaign. Occasional mechanical roughness can also interfere with immersion, particularly when precise interaction is required during stressful situations.

The game requires a VR headset and SteamVR, with standing and room-scale play forming part of its intended design. This is important because VR Amazing Files: Horror Hospital is fundamentally a virtual reality title rather than a conventional PC game with an optional headset mode. Its tracked-controller interactions are central to the experience. Players who enjoy older VR experiments may actually find this simplicity appealing, especially if they prefer puzzle-oriented horror over complicated systems or action-heavy combat.

Steam Deck compatibility is effectively unsupported for normal handheld play because the game requires SteamVR and dedicated VR hardware. Even if the Steam Deck could technically handle certain surrounding software configurations, the game is not designed as a conventional Deck experience and cannot simply be played using the handheld's built-in screen and controls. Anyone purchasing specifically for Steam Deck should therefore treat it as incompatible for practical standalone use.

Overall, VR Amazing Files: Horror Hospital succeeds most when it uses limited ammunition, environmental observation, and physical VR interaction to make a relatively small hospital feel dangerous. The combination of escape-room puzzles and zombies gives it more personality than a basic shooting gallery, while the requirement to conserve ammunition adds welcome tension. Its dated presentation, modest scope, and early-generation VR mechanics prevent it from being an essential horror experience today, but there is still some enjoyment available for players interested in older VR horror games and puzzle-based exploration.

Rating: 5/10
